segments.arabic:
١١٧٤٦- محجنة:
وقيل أم محجن «١»، امرأة سوداء كانت تقمّ المسجد.
وقع ذكرها في الصّحيح بغير تسمية.
وسمّاها يحيى بن أبي أنيسة، وهو متروك، عن علقمة بن مرثد، عن رجل من أهل المدينة، قال: كانت امرأة من أهل المدينة يقال لها محجنة تقمّ المسجد، فتفقّدها النبيّ ﵌، فأخبر أنها قد ماتت، فقال: «ألا آذنتموني بها؟» فخرج فصلّى عليها، وكبّر أربعا.
قال يحيى: وحدّثنا الزّهريّ، عن أبي أمامة بن سهل، عن النّبيّ ﵌ نحوه.
ومن طريق عبد اللَّه بن بريدة، عن أبيه- أنّ النبيّ ﵌ مرّ على قبر حديث عهد بدفن، فقال: «متى دفن هذا؟» فقيل: هذه أم محجن التي كانت مولعة بلقط القذى من المسجد، فقال: «أفلا آذنتموني؟» «٢» قالوا: كنت نائما فكرهنا أن نوقظك ...
الحديث.
segments.english:
11746 — Mihjanah:

It is also said that she was Umm Mihjan,(1) a black woman who used to sweep the mosque.

She is mentioned in al-Sahih without being named.

Yahya ibn Abi Unaysah—who is rejected as a transmitter—named her, narrating from Alqamah ibn Marthad, from a man of Medina, who said: There was a woman of Medina called Mihjanah who used to sweep the mosque. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, noticed her absence and was informed that she had died. He said, “Why did you not notify me about her?” He then went out, prayed over her, and pronounced four takbirs.

Yahya said: al-Zuhri also related to us, from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

Through Abd Allah ibn Buraydah, from his father, it is related that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed by a grave in which someone had recently been buried and said, “When was this one buried?” He was told, “This is Umm Mihjan, who was devoted to picking up refuse from the mosque.” He said, “Why did you not notify me?”(2) They replied, “You were asleep, and we disliked waking you …”

The rest of the hadith.

unresolved.explanation: The canonical text is unvocalized here, and the supplied witnesses do not determine whether the name should be read Mihjanah or Mahjanah. “Mihjanah” is retained provisionally because of the associated designation Umm Mihjan, but the vocalization is not decisive.
